offence_severity: Death penalty (Section 302 IPC) / Life imprisonment (Section 379 IPC)
physical_harm: Death caused by strangulation and mutilation of the body
number_of_offences: Charged under 4 offences, 3 upheld (death penalty and life imprisonment)
motive: Demand for Rs. 40,000/- for construction of shops
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence of eye-witnesses who are reliable and trustworthy, the recovery of the weapon of offence and the vehicle used for carrying the mutilated body, and the 'last seen together' theory.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as reliable and trustworthy, and noted that even if some witnesses turned hostile, their statements partially supported the prosecution case.
post_offence_conduct: The accused absconded immediately after the incident.
trial_duration: Offence: 29th September, 2003; Trial judgment: Not stated; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: July 11, 2012
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Not stated; Counsel for the State: Not stated
investigation_status: FIR lodged, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted and sentenced to death; High Court: Affirmed conviction except for s. 379/34 IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment and fine; Supreme Court: Affirmed High Court's decision
prosecution_argument: The prosecution case is supported by the evidence of eye-witnesses who are reliable and trustworthy. The evidence establishes the 'last seen together' theory and the fact that after the altercation and strangulation of the deceased, the body was recovered in pieces in presence of the witnesses. The prosecution has proved the complete chain of events.
defence_argument: The appellants contended that the case was based on circumstantial evidence without a complete chain of events, that the prosecution case was not reliable due to hostile witnesses, that the accused were not named in the FIR, and that s. 34 IPC was not attracted as there was no common intention and participation by all the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle of 'common intention' under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, emphasizing that for the applicability of this provision, two factors must be established: common intention and participation in the crime. The court also emphasized that the common intention may develop at the spur of the moment between a number of persons based on the facts of the case.
precedent_relied_upon: Mousam Singh a Roy and Ors. v. State of W B. (2003) 12 sec 377; S.K. Yusuf vs. State of West Bengal (2011) 11 SCC 754; Mohd. Azad @ Samin vs. State of West Bengal (2008) 15 SCC 449; State through Central Bureau of Investigation vs. Mahender Singh Dahiya (2011) 3 SCC 109; Rabindra Kumar Pal @ Dara Singh v. Republic of India (2011) 2 sec 44; Govindaraju@ Govinda v. State by Sriramapuram P.S. and Anr. (2012) 4 sec 722; Brathi alias Sukhdev Singh v. State of Punjab (1991) 1 SCC 519; C.Muniappan v. State of Tamil Nadu (2010) 9 SCC 567; Tika Ram v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2007) 15 SCC 760; Sunil Kumar Sambhudayal Gupta (Dr.) vs. State of Maharashtra (2010) 13 SCC 657; Subhash vs. State of Haryana (2011) 2 SCC 715; Lal/an Rai and Others v. State of Bihar (2003) 1 SCC 268; Dharnidhar v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others (2010) 7 SCC 759
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution has been able to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt, the accused persons absconded immediately after the incident, and the evidence establishes that the accused are responsible for the murder of the deceased. The court emphasized that the accused failed to provide any reasonable explanation for the death of the deceased after they were last seen with him.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The conduct of the accused, including absconding immediately after the incident, the recovery of the weapon of offence and the vehicle used for carrying the mutilated body parts of the deceased, and the fact that the accused were present at the scene of occurrence and participated in the crime.
